concepts.title: The Drowned Bathhouse
concepts.idea: The grotto is not a cave at all. It is the city's first public bathhouse, dug in under the outer wall when the cracked cistern above still fed it, abandoned long ago and quietly gardened by the druids. Its old hot room, round plunge basin and cold apse become the three pools, so Hot-Cold is literally the building's floor plan, and Light-Dark is simply where the vault has fallen in versus where it still holds. It is a man-made civic ruin rather than wilderness, which suits a game about recovering what the city forgot, and its symmetry makes the three pools easy to read at a glance.
concepts.must_show: Entrance and way down: top left, a broken arch at the foot of the wall and a wide flight of worn marble steps, with the courtyard stream sliding beside them in a carved gutter. Sunward Basin: front right, the square old hot bath under a fallen patch of vault, in a direct morning sunbeam, steam on the water, orange-gold fish. Spawning Pond: centre, the round basin with a broken fountain stub, ringed with flat stones, lily pads and fry. Shade Pool: back left, in the intact domed apse, with Old Stoic's roots bursting through the dome and trailing into dark green water, frost at the rim. Druids' ledger: open with blank pages on a marble bench between the Spawning Pond and the Sunward Basin, the three-legged stool beside it. Satchel (minerals/auras): on a bronze hook on the nearest column, pale crystals showing. Outflow: back right, a grated drain channel into the dark tunnel of the underground river. Motes drift in the sunbeam; snails on the mosaic edges.
concepts.prompt: A 16:9 concept painting of a forgotten underground bathhouse beneath an old city wall, turned into a living water garden. Elevated three-quarter view down a long vaulted hall of pale limestone. Top left, a broken archway and a wide flight of worn marble steps lead down, a stream sliding beside them in a carved gutter. Front right, a square sunken hot bath under a collapsed patch of vault: morning sunlight pours straight onto it, steam curls off the water, small orange-gold fish glint. Centre, a round basin with a broken fountain stub, ringed with flat stones, lily pads and tiny fry. Back left, in a domed apse that still holds, thick tree roots burst through the ceiling and trail into a dark green pool, frost feathering its rim. Faded turquoise and terracotta mosaic under moss, ferns in cracks, ivy on columns. A three-legged stool, a marble bench with an open ledger of blank cream pages, a leather satchel of pale crystals on a bronze hook. Back right, a grated channel drains into a dark tunnel. Glowing motes drift in the sunbeam. Hand-painted soft cel-shaded storybook illustration, clean ink outlines, serene and unhurried. No people, no text.

concepts.title: The Travertine Well
concepts.idea: A tall natural sinkhole where the courtyard stream drops in and, over centuries, has built cream mineral terraces that step down the shaft like overflowing bowls. The three pools are three terraces at different depths, so Light-Dark becomes height: the Sunward Basin catches the noon shaft at the top, the Spawning Pond rests in the middle, and the Shade Pool sits at the bottom, where the water slips away into the river. The room is a vertical shaft rather than a floor, climbing down Old Stoic's roots is the daily ritual, and the mood is quiet awe rather than snugness.
concepts.must_show: Entrance: upper left, the cave mouth with daylight beyond, the stream pouring from it onto the top terrace. Way down: Old Stoic's roots twisting down the shaft wall as a winding root stair that links all three tiers. Sunward Basin: upper right, the highest terrace, full in the noon shaft from a round opening in the sky, steaming, orange fish. Spawning Pond: middle, the widest and shallowest terrace, glass-still, ringed with flat stones, snails and fry. Shade Pool: bottom left, in cool blue shadow under hanging roots, frost on its edge, its overflow slipping under a low arch into the dark river. Ledger (blank pages), stool and canvas satchel: on a flat root platform beside the Spawning Pond at mid-height, so the work spot sits at the centre of the frame. Motes in the sunbeam. Keep the three tiers clearly separated in height so each pool reads on its own.
concepts.prompt: A 16:9 concept painting of a tall hidden sinkhole grotto where a stream has built cascading terraces of cream mineral stone, like stacked overflowing bowls. Elevated three-quarter view from partway up the shaft, looking down across three tiers. High above, a round opening in the rock lets a single shaft of noon sunlight fall. Upper left, a cave mouth with daylight beyond, the stream spilling from it down the terraces; huge tree roots twist down the shaft wall beside it, forming a winding root stair. Upper right, the highest terrace pool sits full in the sunbeam: warm turquoise water, rising steam, orange fish. Middle, a wide shallow terrace pool, glass-still, ringed with flat stones, snails on its rim and tiny fry. Bottom left, the lowest pool lies in cool blue shadow under a curtain of hanging roots, frost lacing its edge, its water slipping under a low arch into darkness. On a flat root platform beside the middle pool: a three-legged stool, an open ledger of blank cream pages, a canvas satchel. Moss, ferns, glowing motes. Palette of cream, apricot, mineral turquoise and cool blue. Hand-painted soft cel-shaded storybook illustration, clean ink outlines, quiet awe. No people, no text.

concepts.title: The Glow Hollow
concepts.idea: A low, wide, purely natural pocket cave no taller than a cottage room, with no daylight at all. The only light is the pools' own life (glowing motes, luminous plants) and one lantern the druids hang; the Sunward Basin's warmth comes from pale pebbles that soaked up sun high in the city and were carried down, which follows the art bible's rule that warm light is always brought down from above. Each pool's glow shows its state, honey-amber for the light, warm Sunward Basin and ink-indigo for the Shade Pool, so the two axes read as colour in the dark, and the room feels like a hushed secret the player has been trusted with.
concepts.must_show: Entrance and way down: back right, a low cave mouth where the stream trickles in over a lip, with rough-cut steps and a rope rail down to the floor. Sunward Basin: front left, the largest pool, glowing honey-amber from warm pebbles on its bed, steaming, golden fish. Shade Pool: back left, under a curtain of Old Stoic's roots hanging from the low ceiling, deep indigo, frost lace on the rim. Spawning Pond: front centre-right, perfectly still, ringed with flat stones, glowing snails and fry among water plants. Ledger (blank pages), stool and woven satchel: on a flat flowstone ledge right of centre under the hanging iron lantern, the warmest carried light in the room. Outflow: front right, water slipping between stones into a dark crack toward the river. Motes everywhere like slow sparks. The low ceiling edge stays visible at the top of the frame.
concepts.prompt: A 16:9 concept painting of a low natural cave hidden underground, lit only by its own glowing pools and one hanging lantern. Close, elevated three-quarter view, the rounded rock ceiling just visible along the top edge, snug as a burrow. Three scalloped rimstone pools sit in a rippled flowstone floor. Front left, a pool glows warm honey-amber from luminous pebbles on its bed, wisps of steam rising, golden fish circling. Back left, under a curtain of thick tree roots, a pool of deep indigo water, faintly blue, with lacy frost on its rim. Front centre-right, a perfectly still pool ringed with flat stones, glowing snails and tiny fry among water plants. Back right, a low cave mouth where a stream trickles in over a lip, rough steps and a rope rail leading down. On a flat ledge right of centre beneath a hanging iron lantern: a three-legged stool, an open ledger of blank cream pages, a woven satchel. Front right, water slips between stones into a dark crack. Glowing motes float everywhere like slow sparks. Palette of indigo, plum, deep teal, honey and mint. Hand-painted soft cel-shaded storybook illustration, clean ink outlines, hushed and dreamy. No people, no text.

concepts.title: Beneath the Wall, Cut Open
concepts.idea: The grotto drawn as a slice, a block of earth cut open on two faces like a picture-book cross-section. The courtyard is a thin grassy strip on top, and below it snug pool chambers are threaded through Old Stoic's roots and the outer wall's huge foundation stones. The cut makes the room's place in the world readable at a glance (water comes in from the courtyard above and leaves as the river at the bottom), and the druids' homely props make it a lived-in burrow rather than a ruin or a wonder. The camera sits outside the space, which suits a habitat tended like a terrarium.
concepts.must_show: Top: the courtyard strip with the base of Old Stoic's trunk and the stream diving into a cave mouth at the foot of the wall's fitted stones (the entrance). Way down: roots and a wooden ladder from the cave mouth into the chambers. Sunward Basin: upper left chamber, lit by a sunbeam dropping down a narrow shaft from the courtyard, steaming, orange fish. Spawning Pond: middle, the widest chamber, still water ringed with flat stones, snails and fry. Shade Pool: lower right, under the foundation blocks, dark and cool, frost on its rim, overflowing into a tunnel that leaves the cut face as the underground river. Ledger (blank pages) on a root shelf beside the Spawning Pond, the stool beneath it, the satchel on a root peg, one lantern. Old Stoic's roots threading through every chamber. Motes drifting.
concepts.prompt: A 16:9 concept painting of a cutaway diorama: a cube-shaped block of earth, seen from an elevated three-quarter angle and sliced open on its front and side faces to reveal a hidden grotto, like a picture-book cross-section. On top, a strip of grassy courtyard with the base of a huge tree trunk and a stream diving into a cave mouth at the foot of massive fitted wall stones. The tree's roots thread down through layers of loam and clay, forming beams, shelves and a ladder down from the cave mouth. Upper left pocket: a pool lit by a sunbeam falling down a narrow shaft from the courtyard, warm with steam and orange fish. Middle: a wide still pool ringed with flat stones, snails and fry. Lower right, under the foundation blocks: a dark cool pool with frost on its rim, overflowing into a tunnel leaving the cut face as an underground river. A root shelf holds an open ledger of blank cream pages; a stool, a satchel on a root peg, a lantern. Late afternoon light; palette of umber, ochre, moss green and teal. Hand-painted soft cel-shaded storybook illustration, clean ink outlines, snug and curious. No people, no text.

concepts.title: The River Gate at Dawn
concepts.idea: The grotto as the city's quiet back door: a vaulted tunnel at the foot of the outer wall where the underground river leaves through an old water gate, its iron grille rusted open long ago and wound with flowers, while low dawn sun pours in sideways from the wide world beyond. The pools sit on stepped ledges beside the river, warm and bright nearest the outer mouth and cool and shaded deepest inside under the roots, so Light-Dark runs along the tunnel toward the sunrise. It is the only take lit from outside the city and the only one that looks outward, which makes it open and hopeful; it does invent the river leaving through a gate in the wall, so the designer should confirm that fits the lore.
concepts.must_show: Entrance and way down: foreground left, worn steps coming down from a small inner arch (the cave mouth from the courtyard), with the stream trickling beside them. Shade Pool: nearest the viewer, in deep shade under Old Stoic's roots breaking through the vault, frost on its rim. Spawning Pond: midway along the tunnel on a stone ledge, perfectly still, ringed with flat stones, snails and fry. Sunward Basin: far end, nearest the sunlit outer mouth, bright and steaming, orange fish, in the dawn beam. Druids' timber boardwalk along the river, between the Spawning Pond and the viewer, carrying the stool, the open ledger (blank pages) and the satchel on a peg. River: running the length of the tunnel and out through the vine-veiled water gate with its grille open. Motes in the light beams. Keep the tunnel short and wide so the far Sunward Basin stays large and readable against the backlight.
concepts.prompt: A 16:9 concept painting of a hidden vaulted water tunnel at the base of a pale limestone city wall, where an underground river slips out to the world through an old water gate. Elevated three-quarter view from the inner end, looking toward the far mouth: an arch veiled by hanging vines, a rusted iron grille swung open and wound with flowering creepers, low dawn sunlight streaming in sideways through mist. Foreground left, worn stone steps come down from a small arch, a trickling stream beside them. Along the tunnel, stepped stone ledges hold three pools beside a river and a timber boardwalk. Nearest the sunlit mouth, a bright warm pool shimmers with steam and orange fish. Midway, a perfectly still pool ringed with flat stones, snails and fry. Nearest the viewer, in deep shade under thick tree roots breaking through the vault, a dark cool pool rimmed with frost. On the boardwalk: a three-legged stool, an open ledger of blank cream pages, a satchel on a peg. Moss, ferns, glowing motes in the beams. Palette of misty rose, peach, sage and lilac shadow. Hand-painted soft cel-shaded storybook illustration, clean ink outlines, open and hopeful. No people, no text.

concepts.title: Hearth Under the Rafters
concepts.idea: The Apothecary as a cottage herbalist's kitchen. The whole little house is one room open to its steep purple roof, and the brick chimney is its spine, so brewing happens at the hearth like cooking, not wizardry, and a wrong mix costs nothing but a pot to wash. The discovery tree grows as blank cards pinned on string that branches from the chimney across the plaster, so every find visibly adds a twig to the wall, and an empty basket by the door is where the Sanctum's derived ingredients arrive. The emotional note is snug and sheltered: a firelit evening of tinkering at home.
concepts.must_show: Foreground centre: a long oak trestle table holding the four bench tools spaced well apart, left to right: mortar and pestle, magnifying glass on a wooden stand, small lit oil burner, brass balance scales. At the table's right end: the three starting ingredients in three clearly different vessels. They are shown here as an herb bundle, a salt crock and a water jug; swap in whatever the content names. Back wall centre: the brick chimney breast and open hearth with a copper cauldron on a crane, which is the brewing station. The discovery map: a tree of undyed string and blank cards spreading out from the chimney across the back gable wall. Discovery storage: low shelves under the eaves on the left and right, with blank-labelled crocks and jars and deliberate empty gaps for future finds. By the door: an empty wicker basket where ingredients routed from the Sanctum arrive. Herb bunches hang from the rafters as atmosphere only; they must not crowd the table.
concepts.prompt: Concept painting, 16:9: a cozy herbalist's cottage workshop as a dollhouse cutaway, front gable removed: one tall triangular room open to steep dark oak rafters under a plum-purple slate roof. Camera: elevated and nearly frontal, like a stage set. A broad brick chimney breast rises up the middle of the back wall; its hearth holds a low fire and a copper cauldron on an iron crane. Undyed string branches from the chimney across the pale lime plaster like a tree, holding small blank paper cards. Drying herb bunches hang from the rafters. Low shelves under both eaves hold earthenware crocks and glass jars with blank paper labels, and empty gaps. Foreground: a scrubbed oak trestle table with a stone mortar and pestle, a magnifying glass on a wooden stand, a small lit clay oil burner and brass balance scales, spaced apart; at its end, a bundle of fresh green herbs, a crock of coarse white salt and a jug of clear water. An empty wicker basket hangs by the door. Night, lit only by fire: amber and ember light, deep plum shadows, ochre and sage. Hand-painted soft cel-shaded storybook illustration, clean ink outlines. No people, no text.

concepts.title: Glasshouse Against the Wall
concepts.idea: The Apothecary grows and gathers its own matter. The cottage's back opens into a long glass lean-to built against the pale outer city wall, half still-room and half potting shed. The starting ingredients are living and local: a potted herb, water seeping down the wall into a trough, and salt bloomed out of the damp limestone. That grounds the alchemy in the courtyard itself. The discovery tree is pegged up like washing on branching twine, the city's own washing lines turned into a map that lengthens with each find. The emotional note is fresh and quietly hopeful: a dewy blue dawn full of possibility.
concepts.must_show: Foreground, along the near edge: the long potting bench, with the mortar and pestle, a magnifying glass on a jointed brass arm, a spirit lamp under a glass flask, and small balance scales spaced along its length. At the bench end nearest the wall: the three starting ingredients as living sources, a potted herb, a stone trough fed by the wall seep and a dish of salt crust, each with a distinct silhouette. The identities follow the content. Back wall, the city's own near-white limestone: stepped wooden staging with blank-labelled jars, seedling pots and deliberate empty gaps. Above it, the discovery map: blank cards on wooden pegs along twine that branches from a single nail. At the far end (the vanishing point): a squat iron stove and steaming copper kettle beside the brick chimney, which is the brewing station, with the purple roof edge marking where the glasshouse meets the cottage. Optional: a small empty crate at the bench end as the arrival spot for ingredients routed from the Sanctum.
concepts.prompt: Concept painting, 16:9: a long, narrow glasshouse workshop built as a lean-to against a towering wall of pale, near-white limestone blocks. Its roof and front are small leaded glass panes in white-painted timber frames, beaded with dew. Camera: elevated three-quarter view looking diagonally down the room's length, receding to a squat iron stove with a steaming copper kettle beside a brick chimney under a purple roof edge. Along the limestone back wall, stepped wooden staging holds glass jars with blank paper labels, seedling pots and empty gaps. Above, branching twine strung from a single nail carries blank cards on wooden pegs, like a tree made of washing lines. Foreground: a long potting bench with a stone mortar and pestle, a magnifying glass on a jointed brass arm, a spirit lamp under a glass flask, and small balance scales. At the bench's end: a potted green herb, a stone trough fed by water seeping down the wall, and a dish of white salt crust. Early dawn: cool blue-green light, a peach sky above the glass, one warm burner flame. Celadon, sage, cream and terracotta. Hand-painted soft cel-shaded storybook illustration, clean ink outlines. No people, no text.

concepts.title: Noon Shaft Still-Room
concepts.idea: The Apothecary as a tall, two-level still-room built of reused pale city stone. Distilling happens at a brick furnace below, and a wrought-iron gallery of jewel-glass bottles runs above, so the collection literally climbs in tiers as the discovery tree grows: the city's stacked steps brought indoors. The discovery map lies spread on the central table and every experiment is done on top of it, while an empty basket on a pulley drops from the gallery, echoing how everything in the Atrium arrives from above. For a few hours a day the noon shaft through the roof lantern lands on that table, so the emotional note is hushed wonder, the quiet moment a combination comes good.
concepts.must_show: Centre: a heavy walnut table, read from above like a game board, with the discovery map spread across it: a blank parchment chart of empty circles joined by lines. The four bench tools sit on it, toward its corners: mortar and pestle, magnifying glass on an iron arm, small brass burner and fine balance scales. At the table's near corner: the three starting ingredients in three lidded stoneware jars. Give each a different glaze or lid shape so they read apart; the identities follow the content. Ground floor, against one side wall: the brick furnace with a glass alembic dripping into a receiving flask, which is the brewing station, its flue rising into the chimney. Upper level: a wrought-iron gallery along both walls, with blank-labelled cobalt, amethyst and green bottles, pale stoneware jars and deliberate empty spaces, and a wooden ladder up to it. A pulley basket hangs from the gallery rail as the arrival point for ingredients routed from the Sanctum. The light shaft must land on the table, not on the shelves.
concepts.prompt: Concept painting, 16:9: a tall, two-level stone still-room seen as a corner cutaway from a high three-quarter angle, like an open box. Pale, near-white limestone walls; a worn blue-and-white tiled floor. On the ground floor, a brick furnace against one wall carries a large glass alembic dripping into a receiving flask; its flue rises into a brick chimney. Above, a narrow wrought-iron gallery runs along both walls, reached by a wooden ladder, its shelves holding cobalt, amethyst and green glass bottles and pale stoneware jars, all with blank paper labels, and empty spaces. A rope and pulley lowers an empty basket from the gallery rail. Centre: a heavy walnut table with a large blank parchment chart spread across it, drawn as a branching tree of empty circles joined by lines; on it a stone mortar and pestle, a magnifying glass on an iron arm, a small brass burner and fine balance scales. Three lidded stoneware jars stand at the table's corner. Noon: one shaft of white-gold sunlight falls from a roof lantern onto the table; the rest lies in cool slate-blue shade, glass glinting. Hand-painted soft cel-shaded storybook illustration, clean ink outlines. No people, no text.

concepts.title: The Book Amphitheatre
concepts.idea: The floor of the narrow stone house is dug down into a half-round amphitheatre, and every riser is one long curved bookshelf. That makes the Library the tiered city in miniature: tomes come in at the top door, are carried down tier by tier to their genre, and the knowledge gathers at a reading desk at the bottom, the way everything in the Atrium arrives from above. Each tier is one genre band with one long, unbroken run of spines, so the state of the sorting reads at a glance across the whole bowl, and the noon shaft lights the reading desk like a stage spotlight.
concepts.must_show: Five curved shelf tiers facing the camera, from the highest at the back to the lowest at the front. Five suits the painting only; the tier count stays data. Each tier has a blank round stone medallion at its stair end, where the engine draws the sigil or genre tag. A narrow stair runs straight down the centre. The returns crate is lidded wood, sitting on the top step beside the arched entrance at the back centre, with new tomes poking out. The unsorted pile spills from it down the upper steps like scree. The reading desk sits at the front centre on a small round paved floor, with a slanted lectern, an open book with blank pages and a squat iron lamp, inside the light shaft. The glass roof lantern at the top of the frame is the visible light source.
concepts.prompt: 16:9 concept painting of a cozy library interior, hand-painted soft cel-shaded storybook illustration with clean warm-brown ink outlines. Inside a tall, narrow stone house the floor steps down into a half-round amphitheatre of books: five curved stone terraces descend toward the viewer like the seats of an ancient theatre, and the face of every terrace is one long curved bookshelf packed with cloth-bound tomes in muted blue, moss, plum and oatmeal. A blank round stone medallion marks the end of each tier. A narrow stair cuts straight down the middle. At the bottom, on a small round floor of pale paving, stands a reading desk with a slanted lectern holding one open book with blank cream pages, beside a squat iron lamp. On the top step, by an arched doorway, sits a lidded wooden returns crate with new tomes poking out, and a drift of unsorted books spills down the steps like scree. Camera: elevated three-quarter view looking down into the bowl. Light: noon, one soft white shaft from a glass lantern in the steep roof falls onto the desk. Palette: near-white limestone, cool blue-grey shade, deep blue accents. Serene, hushed, orderly. No people, no text.

concepts.title: Under the Blue Roof
concepts.idea: The Library is the city's forgotten attic: the inside of the steep blue roof, where lore that drifted down the tiers has piled up in the rafters, and new tomes come up through a floor hatch from the courtyard. A single lamp at the far end sets the shelving grammar ('oldest nearest the lamp'), so the order shows as a gradient of age down the length of the room. The rainy-night window nook makes opening a tome feel like a small reward, which keeps the cozy loop worth doing with zero mystery progress.
concepts.must_show: Two runs of low built-in shelves along the left and right eaves, divided into bays, each bay with a small blank wooden tag hanging on twine (the slot for the genre or sigil tag). Books look crisper near the camera and more worn and patched toward the lamp. In the near foreground, lower centre, an open square trapdoor with a rope-and-pulley wicker basket rising through it carrying new books: that is the returns. At the far end, in the centre, a cushioned window-seat reading nook under the round gable window, with a slanted reading stand, one open book with blank pages, and the brass oil lamp as the only warm light. Beside the nook, a stool holding a pencil jar, a teacup and a biscuit tin with crumbs. The indigo-painted rafters frame the whole top of the image.
concepts.prompt: 16:9 concept painting of a snug attic library, hand-painted soft cel-shaded storybook illustration with clean warm-brown ink outlines. A long, narrow loft under a steep pitched roof: the rafters and roof boards are painted deep indigo blue, and rain streaks a round window in the far gable. Low built-in bookshelves run along both sides under the eaves, divided into bays, each bay hung with a small blank wooden tag on twine; the shelves are full of cloth and leather tomes that grow older and more patched toward the far end. Beneath the round window is a cushioned window-seat nook with a quilt, a slanted reading stand holding one open book with blank cream pages, and a brass oil lamp, the only warm light, glowing amber. In the near floorboards a square trapdoor stands open, and a wicker basket on a rope and pulley rises through it carrying new books. A pencil jar, teacup and crumb-dusted biscuit tin sit on a stool. Camera: elevated three-quarter view from the near end, looking down the length of the loft. Rainy night, warm and hidden. Palette: honey oak, indigo, lamp amber, moss green. No people, no text.

concepts.title: The Sorting Office
concepts.idea: The Library is the city's old post and lost-property room: books drop in through a slot from the courtyard like letters, and classifying becomes the hands-on fun of a mail sorter filling a wall of pigeonholes. The grid shows the shelving state at a glance, because every empty cubby is a visible job left to do. A bookwheel holds several open tomes side by side, which gives the Library's lens (classification and cross-reference: what cites what) a physical object the player can use.
concepts.must_show: Across the centre and back of the frame, a wall of square pigeonhole shelves in five tall columns. Each column has a differently painted frame and a blank enamel plaque at its top for the engine's genre or sigil tag; the column count and colours are a proposal, not a commitment. A rolling ladder on a brass rail. The cubbies are partly filled, with many empty. On the right wall, a brass-lipped slot through to the courtyard, with a canvas chute sliding new tomes into a wheeled wicker hamper: that is the returns. In the foreground, a long oak trestle table holding stacks of unsorted books, string and a pencil jar. On the left, the reading place: a tall wooden bookwheel with several small lecterns, each holding an open book with blank pages, beside a worn armchair. One tall arched window is the source of the raking late-afternoon sun.
concepts.prompt: 16:9 concept painting of a library sorting hall, hand-painted soft cel-shaded storybook illustration with clean warm-brown ink outlines. A tall, narrow room of pale limestone, seen like a stage set with the near wall removed, from slightly above, almost square-on. The whole back wall is one grid of square wooden pigeonhole shelves in five tall columns, each column's frame painted a different soft colour (sage, slate blue, ochre, plum, moss) with a blank enamel plaque at its top, and a wooden rolling ladder on a brass rail. Some cubbies hold books; many wait empty. In the right wall a brass-lipped slot opens to the courtyard, and a canvas chute slides new tomes into a big wheeled wicker hamper. In the foreground a long oak trestle table holds stacks of unsorted books, string and a pencil jar. On the left stands a wooden bookwheel, a tall rotating wheel of small lecterns, each holding an open book with blank cream pages, beside a worn armchair. Late afternoon sun through one tall arched window rakes across the room in long warm stripes through drifting dust. Palette: cream, sage, warm peach stone, brass, deep blue. Busy, playful, satisfying. No people, no text.

concepts.title: The Old Bathhouse Dome
concepts.idea: The Sanctum was once the city's forgotten hot bath. The Keeper has turned its round domed chamber into a study: the dry central plunge basin becomes the Reconstitution Circle and the old bathers' alcoves become the catalogue of discoveries. This ties restoration to the courtyard's own water lore (the cracked cistern above) as refilling something that was emptied. A single open floor under a dome pierced with glass bull's-eyes keeps every station readable at a glance in scattered coins of daylight.
concepts.must_show: Reconstitution Circle: the dry round plunge basin at the room's centre, two shallow steps down, with a plain pale stone rim that glows faintly and a tray of dull remnants on its step. Balance: a verdigris-bronze beam scale with two shallow pans on a stone plinth, to the right of the basin. Journal: a thick cloth-bound book open on a tiled lectern, front left, nearest the camera. Tagging: blank paper tags hung along an old bronze towel rail on the left wall. Catalogue of discoveries: arched bathers' alcoves round the back wall, one found object in each. Tool assembly: a marble slab bench at the right rear with parts and a half-built instrument. The entrance is behind the camera.
concepts.prompt: 16:9 concept painting, hand-painted soft cel-shaded storybook illustration with clean warm-brown ink outlines. Inside an old round bathhouse chamber within a domed sandstone tower, now a quiet study of curiosities. Elevated three-quarter view from inside the doorway, the whole round room in frame, the dome's underside filling the top third. Dozens of small round glass skylights in the dome scatter coins of bright late-morning daylight across floor and walls. Centre: two shallow steps lead down into a dry round plunge basin with a plain pale stone rim, glowing faintly; a tray of dull grey fragments rests on its step. Right: a verdigris-bronze beam balance with two shallow pans on a stone plinth. Front left: a thick cloth-bound book open to blank cream pages on a tiled lectern. Along the left wall, a bronze towel rail hung with blank paper tags. Arched alcoves around the back wall each hold one found object: a shell, a seed pod, a stone. Right rear: a marble slab bench with tools and a half-built brass-and-wood instrument. Palette: chalky cream sandstone, faded turquoise tile, soft coral terracotta, cool blue shade. Airy, sunlit, gently delighted. Plain floor, no symbols. No people, no text.

concepts.title: The Lamplit Stacked Tower
concepts.idea: A narrow three-storey tower shown as a dollhouse cutaway, where each floor is one stage of the Sanctum loop: tools are assembled at the bottom, discoveries are tagged and catalogued in the middle, and objects are weighed and restored under the dome. A rope-and-pulley dumbwaiter lifts objects between floors, so unlocking reads as a climb toward the Circle. The stacked lamplit rooms against the night give a busy, homey workshop warmth that echoes the city's own stacked tiers.
concepts.must_show: The whole tower from top to bottom, with its front half cut away. Ground floor: the tool-assembly workbench with a vise, a pegboard, a parts tray and a half-built instrument, plus a small iron stove. Middle floor: the journal open on a slanted writing desk under a hanging lamp, beside a wall of small drawers (the catalogue); a blank tag is tied to each drawer knob for taxonomy tagging. Top floor, under the dome: the Reconstitution Circle as a plain hexagonal brass-rimmed plate inlaid in the floorboards beneath a round window, with the tall hanging beam balance beside it. A spiral stair on one side and a rope dumbwaiter on the other link the floors.
concepts.prompt: 16:9 concept painting, hand-painted soft cel-shaded storybook illustration with clean warm-brown ink outlines. A narrow round sandstone tower with a small dome, shown as a dollhouse cutaway with its front half removed, framed straight-on from slightly above so all three floors show at once. Night: each floor glows with its own hanging oil lamp against a deep indigo sky. Ground floor: a workbench with a vise, a pegboard of tools, a tray of springs and lenses, and a half-built brass-and-wood instrument, beside a little iron stove. Middle floor: a slanted writing desk holding a thick open journal with blank cream pages, and a wall of small wooden drawers, each with a blank paper tag tied to its knob. Top floor, under the dome: a plain hexagonal brass-rimmed plate set into the floorboards, softly glowing in moonlight from a round window; beside it a tall hanging beam balance with two pans. A wooden spiral stair climbs one side; a rope-and-pulley dumbwaiter the other. Palette: indigo, lamp amber, ochre sandstone, bottle-green woodwork, mellow brass. Busy, homey, tinkering warmth. No symbols on the floor. No people, no text.

concepts.title: The Spiral of Findings
concepts.idea: One continuous ramp coils up the inside wall like a snail shell, and every discovery is shelved along it in the order it was found. The catalogue becomes a walkable timeline of the player's journal, running from the Circle at the heart to the balance on the top landing. Ferns and ivy from the overgrown courtyard creep in at the windows, and the rainy light makes it a hushed room for slowing down, thinking and tagging.
concepts.must_show: The camera looks down into the coil, with the top landing nearest. Reconstitution Circle: a plain ring of pale flat stones set in moss at the bottom centre, glowing faintly, with a basket of dull remnants beside it. Journal: a large open book on a low reading table by the Circle, with a cushioned chair and a small iron stove (the only warm light). Catalogue and tagging: small niches along the ramp, each holding one discovery with a blank paper tag on twine. Tool assembly: a workbench on a mid-ramp landing. Balance: a wooden beam balance with brass pans on the top landing, in the foreground.
concepts.prompt: 16:9 concept painting, hand-painted soft cel-shaded storybook illustration with clean warm-brown ink outlines. Interior of a round sandstone tower seen from high above at a steep three-quarter angle, as if the dome were lifted off, looking down into the room. A gentle wooden-railed ramp coils down the inside wall like a snail shell, lined with small niches each holding one found curiosity: a feather, a seed pod, a stone, each with a blank paper tag on twine. At the bottom centre, a plain ring of pale flat stones set into soft moss glows faintly, a basket of dull grey fragments beside it. Near the ring: a low reading table with a large open book of blank cream pages, a cushioned chair, and a little iron stove glowing amber. On a mid-ramp landing, a workbench holds tools and a half-assembled brass-and-wood instrument. On the top landing in the foreground stands a wooden beam balance with two brass pans. Ferns and ivy creep in at the narrow windows, their glass streaked with rain. Palette: sage, moss green, rose-grey sandstone, plum cloth, one spot of amber. Hushed, snug, rainy-afternoon calm. No symbols. No people, no text.
